notes.title: Anti-Cheat Protection Is Not Registered in Production
notes.problem: AntiCheatManager still defines Creative/Spectator correction for non-admin players, but the v1.1.3 production bootstrap does not import or instantiate it. The current lobby owner now independently normalizes ordinary participants to Adventure, so this module is dead/overlapping protection rather than evidence that lobby role normalization is missing.
notes.action: Decide whether AntiCheatManager remains an intended defense-in-depth owner. If not, remove the dead module; if it is required, register it without duplicating the active ArenaService role policy.

evidence.finding: v1.1.3 main.js still does not register AntiCheatManager, while ArenaService.normalizeLobbyRole() now sets ordinary lobby participants to Adventure and disables mayfly.

notes.title: Correct the Daylight-Cycle GameRules Property Name
notes.problem: Build & Decode intends to keep daylight cycling disabled. In v1.1.3, WorldData still uses the key doDaylightCycle while the @minecraft/server GameRules property is doDayLightCycle, so the setup code does not reliably own/reassert that rule if world state changes later.
notes.action: Correct the existing WorldData/WorldManager gamerule key to doDayLightCycle and keep the same world-setup owner. Do not create a second gamerule authority.

notes.title: Clarify Whether Guessers Should Receive Mayfly During Active Rounds
notes.problem: In v1.1.3, the active-round role application still enables mayfly for every playing participant, including Adventure-mode guessers. Current artifact evidence is insufficient to classify this as a defect, but it materially changes how guessers can move and view the build.
notes.action: Confirm the intended guesser movement policy. If flight is builder-only, scope mayfly to builders in both activateRound() and reconnect/applyRole(); otherwise document that guesser flight is intentional.

evidence.finding: activateRound() sets builders to Creative and guessers to Adventure, then applies 'ability @s mayfly true' to every playing participant.

notes.title: Temporary Debug Picker Is Still Included in Release
notes.problem: The v1.1.3 production entrypoint imports scripts/dev/debug-stick.js on every world load. The module identifies itself as a standalone temporary coordinate picker and registers block-interaction and script-event diagnostics. Its interactive paths are explicitly admin-gated, so current selected-artifact evidence does not justify a gameplay BUG.
notes.action: Remove the temporary debug picker from the production bootstrap when it is no longer required, or make its release inclusion an explicit maintained developer capability. Keep the existing explicit admin permission gate if the tool remains shipped.

evidence.finding: main.js imports ./dev/debug-stick.js unconditionally. The module calls itself a temporary coordinate picker and registers interaction/status/export diagnostics; all actionable paths check PermissionData.isAdmin(player).

notes.title: Entity Setup Script Event Has No Explicit Permission Gate
notes.problem: SetupManager handles the setup:entity script event by killing and respawning configured setup entities, but the handler does not check the source against the canonical PermissionData admin owner. Current selected-artifact evidence proves the missing explicit gate, but does not prove that an ordinary player can invoke the script event in the delivered runtime.
notes.action: Route setup:entity through the existing admin permission owner before mutating world entities. Do not rely on implicit command/runtime reachability as the only privilege boundary.

evidence.finding: SetupManager subscribes to scriptEventReceive and executes setupEntities(event.sourceEntity) for setup:entity without PermissionData.isAdmin or another explicit permission check.

notes.title: Player Initialization Properties Are Written but Never Consumed
notes.problem: WelcomeManager writes one world dynamic property named player_<scoreboardParticipantId> containing player name/id data for initialized players. The v1.1.3 production scripts contain no reader or cleanup path for those properties, so the records persist as orphaned per-player state.
notes.action: Remove the unused player_<participantId> persistence if it has no release purpose, or give it one explicit reader and lifecycle owner with bounded cleanup. Do not keep write-only per-player world properties indefinitely.

evidence.finding: savePlayerData() writes player_<participantId>. Full production-script search finds no getDynamicProperty/read path for that namespace and no deletion path.

notes.title: Legacy Capacity and Timing Config Is Still Shipped but Unused
notes.problem: GuessTheBuildData still declares minPlayers, maxPlayers, roundStartCountdown, and lobby.waitingTime, while v1.1.3 runtime admission and timing use ArenaConfig.RULES. Full production-script search finds no consumer for those GameData fields.
notes.action: Remove the unused GameData capacity/timing declarations or route the active gameplay owner through one canonical configuration source. Keep one editable authority for each capacity/timing concept.

evidence.finding: GameData.minPlayers/maxPlayers/roundStartCountdown/lobby.waitingTime have no production consumers; RULES.minPlayers/maxPlayers and active arena countdown owners are used instead.
